candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest classified this binary as MALWARE with probability 1.0000, and all 20 top SHAP features push toward cryptojacking (+0.0066 to +0.0115). No single feature dominates. The contributions are spread evenly, so the verdict rests on the overall opcode-sequence profile. Most of the high-frequency n-grams are generic stack and call-convention patterns: CALL PUSH (0.0354), MOV PUSH (0.0421), PUSH CALL (0.0505), ADD PUSH, SUB PUSH, POP PUSH, and MOV LEAVE. On their own they are not specific to mining. Their combined, consistently positive SHAP weight suggests a code layout the model associates with its malware class, such as call-heavy code with many prologue/epilogue and argument-setup sequences. The rarer n-grams are more suggestive. CMP SHLD (+0.008157) involves a double-precision shift, which can appear in multi-word or bit-manipulation arithmetic. SBB INC (+0.009395) and SHL NEG (+0.006918) involve carry or shift arithmetic. POP XOR (+0.011499, the top feature), POP OR, POP SUB, POP LEA and PUSH RET are unusual register-restore and logic transitions that may reflect hand-tuned or obfuscated code. The evidence contains no function names, API calls, or strings, so I cannot tie any n-gram to a specific mining routine. The tier is therefore based on the model's certainty and the breadth of agreeing features, not on a confirmed mining algorithm.
